newsitem.title: CHILE: Entergy, Endesa to build Chilean plant.
newsitem.headline: Entergy, Endesa to build Chilean plant.

text.p: U.S. firm Entergy Corp and Chile's Empresa Nacional de Electricidad, or Endesa, will team up to build the San Isidro power plant near Santiago starting in December, Entergy said.

The plan calls for building a 370 megawatt plant near the town of Quillota, about two hour's drive north of Santiago, in Entergy's first major power investment in Chile, said the company in a statement.
The $200 million dollar project will get underway in December and begin commercial operations in October 1998, said the statement.
Endesa will hold 75 percent of the property of the San Isidro project, and Entergy the rest, it said.

Entergy and Endesa have acted as partners in two much larger projects, neither in Chile, the statement quoted Entergy president Ed Lupberger as saying. Both are partners in Peru's 639 megawatt Edegel power generator and in the 1,260 megawatt Costanera plant in Argentina.
Entergy and subsidiaries distribute power services to 2.4 million consumers in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Texas, the statement said.
